solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A number hugging tree, dull yes?

indicators.note: the number wraps its arms around the tree and the dull finish, so those go inside it

parts.note: five is a number
a fir is a conifer tree
mat (or matt) describes a dull, unshiny finish

explanation.surface: A puzzled questioner asks whether some number embracing a tree is dull, and gets a yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dull yes?' reads as one phrase, but 'dull' belongs to the wordplay and 'yes' alone is the definition; 'hugging' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An affirmative reply is an agreeing one, so the word stands for the single reply of assent.

clue.text: Cross about our tenant, wife gives curse

indicators.note: the crossing word goes round the rest, so it encloses them

parts.note: to ford is to cross a river by wading
taken as written
a letter is one who lets property; the setter uses it loosely for the occupant renting it

explanation.surface: An angry landlord, cross about a tenant, hears the tenant's wife swear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like anger but is the verb to wade a river; 'about' is the container signal. A letter strictly lets property out, so calling the tenant that is a stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: A swear word such as an expletive is commonly called by this phrase, from the length of the classic obscenities.

clue.text: Extreme characters in fine club

definitions.meaning: the end letters of the word fine are F and E, and Fe is the chemical symbol of this metal
a golf club with an angled metal head

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is cryptic: F and E, the outside letters of 'fine', form the chemical symbol Fe, so it names the metal rather than giving its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Golfers carry numbered clubs of this kind, and Fe is the element's symbol from Latin ferrum.

clue.text: Water spoiled suit with further clothing

indicators.note: the extra word dresses the jumbled letters, wrapping round them

parts.note: more means further or additional

indicators.note: a spoiled suit is ruined, so its letters are messed into a new order

explanation.surface: Water ruined a suit, and then more clothing too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothing' looks like garments but is the container signal; 'spoiled' makes ISTU from the suit's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Dampness or wetness in the air or a material is water in small quantity.

clue.text: Fastener caught up on broken leg

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: got means caught, as in got a cold

indicators.note: a broken leg is out of shape, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fastener caught on someone's broken leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns GOT into TOG; 'broken' turns LEG into GLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A short bar or peg passed through a loop, as on a duffel coat, is a fastener of this type.

clue.text: Bottle important, having lost heart

indicators.note: losing the heart means the central letter of the word goes

parts.note: vital means important or essential

explanation.surface: An important bottle has lost its courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having lost heart' removes T, the middle of VITAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A small glass container for medicine or scent is a little bottle.

clue.text: Hot dish cold, hero getting stick about flavour, ultimately

parts.note: chill means cold
an icon is an idolised figure, a hero

indicators.note: the stick goes around that final letter

parts.note: a cane is a walking stick

indicators.note: ultimately means take the very end of the word flavour

explanation.surface: A hot dish goes cold while a hero brandishes a stick about the flavour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives R, the end of 'flavour', which 'about' puts inside CANE.
explanation.definitionFit: This spicy stew of minced beef, beans and peppers is a well-known hot dish.

clue.text: Primate overcoming slender attacker drinking knockout tea

indicators.note: in a down clue the ape sits over, on top of, the rest

parts.note: orang is short for orang-utan, an ape

indicators.note: the sword swallows the knockout, taking it inside

parts.note: an epee is a thin fencing sword
KO is the abbreviation for a knockout in boxing

explanation.surface: An ape sees off a thin assailant drinking a knockout cup of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'slender attacker' is a fencing sword, not a person; 'drinking' is the container signal and 'overcoming' places the ape on top in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A high-grade black Indian or Sri Lankan leaf is sold under this name, a variety of tea.

clue.text: Life's work for one?

parts.note: life's work suggests a career, but read literally it is a person whose work is writing up their own life

explanation.walkthrough: 'Life's work' sounds like a career's achievement; here it is the writing of one's own life story.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer of a memoir of their own life produces a book about themself, the work of a lifetime.

clue.text: Truth hard to believe, spit over cliff

indicators.note: in a down clue the first word stands over the second

parts.note: the spit or spitting image of someone is their double
a bluff is a steep cliff or headland

explanation.surface: A truth hard to believe: someone spat over a cliff.
explanation.definitionFit: This ruse is telling the truth in the hope that the listener, expecting deceit, will disbelieve it.

clue.text: European city not seldom, regularly seen

indicators.note: regularly means take every other letter of the words not seldom

explanation.surface: A European city is often visited, not seldom seen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the 2nd, 4th, 6th and 8th letters of 'not seldom'.
explanation.definitionFit: Norway's capital is a city of northern Europe.

clue.text: One processes whisky to this day

definitions.meaning: a distilling apparatus in which whisky is made
even now, as in she lives there yet

explanation.definitionFit: A distillery's apparatus is one sense, and the adverb meaning even now is the other.

clue.text: Ungulate dropping back in style

indicators.note: the antelope loses its back end, its last letter

parts.note: an eland is a large African antelope, a hoofed mammal

explanation.surface: An antelope falling behind still moves with style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping back' removes D, the last letter of ELAND.
explanation.definitionFit: Flair or dash, borrowed from French, is a kind of style.

clue.text: Nerve — one of two on face

definitions.meaning: either fleshy side of the face below the eyes

explanation.definitionFit: Impudence is one meaning; the other is a fleshy side of the face, of which everyone has a pair.

clue.text: Painter of popes, a degree blue

parts.note: a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a degree
blue is the colour of the UK Conservative party, abbreviated Con

explanation.surface: A painter of popes holds a degree and is a bit sad.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue stands for Conservative because that is the British party's colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Francis Bacon, the Irish-born British painter, made a famous series of screaming popes after Velázquez.

clue.text: Schubert played for purveyors of the flesh

indicators.note: the composer's name is played about with, rearranging its letters

explanation.surface: Schubert's music is played to meat sellers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'played' rearranges SCHUBERT.
explanation.definitionFit: Shopkeepers who sell meat are purveyors of animal flesh.

clue.text: Infant finally cradled by inexperienced mother

indicators.note: the inexperienced word holds the letter inside, as a baby is cradled

parts.note: naive means inexperienced or unworldly

indicators.note: finally means take the last letter of the word infant

explanation.surface: A baby is held at last by its inexperienced young mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives T, the end of 'Infant', and 'cradled by' puts it inside NAIVE. 'mother' is adjectival, as in mother tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: One's mother country or mother tongue is the land or language of one's birth.

clue.text: Pro has messed up since, on scientific investigation

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase, concerning scientific investigation

parts.note: for means in favour of, pro

indicators.note: the word since is messed up, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A professional has bungled a scientific inquiry ever since.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pro' looks like a professional but means in favour of; 'messed up' makes ENSIC from the letters of 'since'.
explanation.definitionFit: This adjective describes the application of science to crime investigation, as in a lab's evidence work.

clue.text: One after kiss for team?

definitions.meaning: a kiss is written X, the Roman ten; one, I, after it makes XI
a football or cricket side has this many players

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition works in Roman numerals: X then I reads XI.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket and football sides are called by their player count; and XI in Roman numerals is the same number.

clue.text: Second, not first number that is unmelodic

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second
one is the first number when counting

explanation.surface: A runner-up, not the first number, sings without melody.
explanation.definitionFit: Speech or singing on a single unchanging pitch has no tune, so it lacks melody.

clue.text: Cake remains? Good Lord!

definitions.meaning: the small fragments left after a cake is eaten
a mild British exclamation of surprise

explanation.definitionFit: Leftover morsels of cake are one sense; the other is a mild exclamation of surprise, common in Britain.

clue.text: Grass skirts of women on half of lads

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after
half of means the first two of the four letters of lads
the skirts or edges of a word are its outside letters

explanation.surface: Grass skirts for women are worn by half of the lads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass skirts' reads as a garment, but the split falls after 'Grass'; 'skirts of' takes the outside letters and 'half of' the front half.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretch of mown turf in a garden is an area of grass.

clue.text: Sign one is overwhelmed by God

indicators.note: the numeral is swamped by the god, so it goes inside

parts.note: Ares is the Greek god of war
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A sign that one is overwhelmed by God.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is overwhelmed by' puts I inside ARES.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ram is the first of the twelve star signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: What inspires confidence at first, love for beautiful nymph

indicators.note: to inspire is to breathe in, so the first word takes in the letter

parts.note: eh? is said for what? when asking for something to be repeated

indicators.note: at first means take the opening letter of the word confidence

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: Something that inspires early confidence is love for a beautiful nymph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inspires' puts C, from 'confidence' 'at first', inside EH; then O follows.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the mountain nymph pined for Narcissus until only her voice remained.

clue.text: Stop question, then answer

parts.note: who? is a question word

explanation.surface: Stop asking questions and give an answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This command to a horse tells it to halt, and more widely tells anyone to stop.

clue.text: Spring, time for quarrel

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring

explanation.surface: Spring is a time for a falling-out.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief petty argument is a small quarrel.

clue.text: River top, stream beaten usually

parts.note: the Forth is a Scottish river

indicators.note: beaten means knocked into a new shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A river with its top stream beaten, as is usual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top stream' looks like a river's upper course, but 'beaten' makes it EMOSTPART; the Forth is the Scottish river flowing into the Firth of Forth.
explanation.definitionFit: This phrase means in most cases, so it stands for generally or as a rule.

clue.text: Bloomer on ship getting delivery grounded?

parts.note: a bloomer is a flower, something that blooms, here a daisy
a cutter is a small single-masted sailing vessel

explanation.surface: A flower on board a ship is delivered on the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder; it is a flower. In cricket, a ball bowled is a delivery, and one that skims along the grass earns this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricketers use this name for a bowled ball that runs along the ground, low enough to clip the flowers.
